correctness.rationale: Every populations of at most four individuals case is classified with no metric assumption, yielding the only nontrivial four-individual covariance \(d(B,C)/12\). For any two or more singleton species, two omission classes give an explicit elementary covariance identity \(4(2V-(r-2)U)/[(r+2)^2r(r+1)]\), independently checked by labeled-subset rational enumeration for 40 arbitrary matrices and 150 ultrametrics. Substitution proves the ratio threshold for all integers three or more singleton species, and r=3 supplies five individuals with covariance \(-1/25\). At sample size two covariance is positive by a directly exhibited pair event; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The dependence of two standard biodiversity statistics at the same random survey effort is structurally different from deterministic monotonicity and expected rarefaction. A sharp lower population boundary, exact general near-census mean-distance threshold, and instability of the positive covariance intuition at arbitrarily small ultrametric departure from a star make a meaningful interpretability result, not a lookup or arbitrary isolated parameter case. A near-census Rao covariance can be negative precisely where analogous rooted Faith diversity covariances have a nonnegative boundary; standard Gini–Simpson is the equal-distance specialization. The numerical witness is embedded in an unrestricted analytical family.
